notes.claim: A transformer has a no-load loss, present whenever it is energised whatever the load, and a load loss that goes with the square of the loading.
The open-circuit (no-load) test measures the iron loss; the short-circuit test, run at rated current, measures the copper loss.
A good real transformer can have losses as low as 1% of the transmitted power.

sources.title: 15.6 Transformers - University Physics Volume 2 | OpenStax
sources.quote: A good transformer can have losses as low as 1% of the transmitted power, so this is not a bad assumption.

sources.title: TRANSFORMER LOSS ENERGY SAVINGS FLEXIBILITY
sources.quote: Transformers have both a no-load loss, that is present whenever the transformer is energized and is independent of the load level, and a load loss that is related to the transformer loading squared.

sources.title: Short-circuit testing | Rohde & Schwarz
sources.quote: an open-circuit test measures the iron loss under no-load conditions

sources.title: Part 4 – Transformer Testing – PEG-3722 Electrotechnology
sources.quote: The short-circuit test is conducted to determine the copper losses of a transformer. It involves simulating a full-load condition by short-circuiting the secondary winding.
